content:
If you've just bought a new Mac, like the recently released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you might be looking for a new external monitor.

Here are my recommendations, covering various product categories, price points, and more.

The best external monitors for Mac

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best monitors on the market, you can't leave out Apple's Studio Display. Although it's a bit pricey, it has beautiful Apple design and a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts display color temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

Studio Display is available in multiple configurations at different prices, listed below. If you want an iMac-like experience with your Mac, the Apple Studio Display is the best choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt and height adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt and height adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

Studio Display XDR was released earlier this year and has several major advantages over the standard Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: SDR up to 1,000 nits; HDR peak up to 2,000 nits
  • Color support: P3 and Adobe RGB wide color gamut, supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz, supporting Adaptive Sync
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, these advantages come at a price—it's more expensive than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor is a great choice for Mac users, featuring a 4K OLED panel. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn switched to it and said, "Using it with my Mac mini for the past few months has been a real treat."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although it doesn't offer the 5K or 6K fine resolution of other models on this list, you can enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks, better color reproduction, and contrast.

Buy Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K is LG's high-end evolution in the monitor business. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels. It also has plenty of ports. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • True Tone technology: None; supports auto brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

LG UltraFine 6K purchase link:

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin got hands-on with this one and it caught my attention right away. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K display offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) at the same 27-inch size, but at half the price of the Studio Display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, supporting Adaptive-Sync
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C supporting DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Watch Jeff's full review for all the details. If you want a 5K display for your Mac, the Asus ProArt is truly hard to beat.

Asus ProArt 5K Display purchase link:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you want a larger, higher-resolution option, Asus has you covered too. The new Asus ProArt Display 6K (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly great value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, supporting Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connectivity, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

The best part of the ASUS ProArt 6K Display might just be its price. It's significantly cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K monitors on the market.

ASUS ProArt 6K Display purchase link:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another solid option for pairing with a new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient light
  • Ports: One USB-C supporting 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K purchase link:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Monitor

This might be my current favorite pick. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes packed with Mac-friendly features, and its biggest highlight is, of course, the sharp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: Typical and peak 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4, one downstream Thunderbolt 4, one upstream USB-C, one downstream USB-C, three USB-A, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with customizable control buttons

BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor purchase link:

See more details in our full review: BenQ 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 Designer Monitor is a True Rival to Apple Studio Display

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor

If you're looking for a 32-inch monitor priced under $1,000 for your new Mac, this is one of the most attractive options out there. The biggest downside is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. But it offers plenty of port options and a 32-inch panel for under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C, three USB-A, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt monitor purchase link:

See more details in our full review: Should 32-inch 4K Mac Monitors Really Have Been Ruled Out from the Start?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultra-Wide Monitor

If you want to pair an ultra-wide monitor with your Mac, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options out there. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch screen. Plus, plenty of ports, a matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz, supporting VRR
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C, five USB-A, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultra-wide monitor purchase link:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

Looking to enter the ultra-wide monitor market at a lower price? The Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is one option, currently at nearly half price. It may not have every fancy feature, but you still get a 34-inch ultra-wide curved monitor with full port connectivity, including a Thunderbolt 4 port that supports power delivery.

  • Display: 34-inch ultra-wide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature, offering an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits.
  • Webcam: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0, one RJ45 Ethernet, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC purchase link:

Conclusion

These are just some of the best external monitor options to pair with a new Mac. They all feature excellent macOS integration, rich connectivity options, and unique sizes and form factors.

Have you recently bought a new Mac? Which monitor are you pairing with it? Feel free to share in the comments.
